name: Licensed music streaming
title: Why Napster failed, and when music streaming became viable
question: Why did Napster fail, and when did music streaming become viable?
answer: Napster (1999) proved that tens of millions of people wanted any song, instantly. Courts shut it down in 2001 because it had no licences. Spotify (2006) waited for licences: it launched in Sweden in 2008 and in the US in July 2011 after deals with the major labels. The binding constraint was legal permission, not technology.
verdict_reason: Label licences for on-demand streaming arrived 2008-2011; Spotify launched as they did.

constraint.name: Label licences for on-demand streaming
constraint.detail: The technology worked in 1999; the right to stream the catalogue did not exist.

crossing.text: Spotify signs the major US labels and launches in the US in July 2011.

graveyard.name: Napster
graveyard.how: Shut by court injunction, July 2001 (A&M Records v. Napster)

evidence.text: The Ninth Circuit upheld the injunction in A&M Records, Inc. v. Napster, Inc. (2001).
